doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Getting drafted while working with Lorenzo Flennoy
summary: Working with Lorenzo Flennoy's band, Hamilton was drafted around the time of Pearl Harbor and sent with two others to Fort McClellan, Alabama.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Okay, let’s stop before we -- because the Army is a whole other thing. You got drafted so if you were 19, that’s 1940.
Right, and I got drafted I think in ‘40 or ‘41.
Okay, so maybe early ‘41 before you turned 20, you were drafted.
So we’re talking about 1940. America’s not even in the war yet.
America is not even in the war yet.
The hell we weren’t. We were in the war.
In 1940? Well Pearl Harbor is December 7, 1941.
So December 8th is when America declares war on Japan and Germany.
Whenever that time was. You know, the point is this, whenever war was, I was working with Lorenzo Flennoy at that time. You ever heard of Joe Comfort?

Me, and Joe Comfort, and James Nelson, Hawk, Lorenzo, myself on drums and Doris Lathy on guitar. Anyway to make a long story short, I got drafted. There was only three of us. They sent us to Fort McLellan, Alabama. Me, Joe (Unintelligible), I forget this other guy’s name, but anyway they sent us there. Like I said, it’s the first time I’d ever seen that many black soldiers.
Because there’s still a segregated army if we’re talking about the early ‘40s, right.
